title: Meghalaya — State GK
why: Meghalaya is the one block of the GK paper that every local rival studies, so it decides ranks: IPO 2022 even used a Tripura festival (Garia Puja) as a Meghalaya trap. Expect 5–8 of the 50 GK questions on formation dates, district HQs, festivals, freedom fighters, records, GI tags and 2025–26 state news. The same facts return in the Personal Interview, where an officer of the State is expected to know the State.

lessons.title: Formation, polity & the Sixth Schedule
lessons.body:
### How Meghalaya became a state — "69 → 70 → 72"

| Step | Fact |
|---|---|
| Constitutional enabler | **22nd Amendment Act, 1969** inserted **Art. 244A** — Parliament may create an *autonomous State within Assam* (assent 25 Sep 1969) |
| Autonomous State | **Assam Reorganisation (Meghalaya) Act, 1969** → autonomous state inside Assam from **2 April 1970** |
| Full statehood | **North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971** → full state on **21 January 1972** (*Meghalaya Day*). **Manipur and Tripura** also became states the same day |
| Carved from | Two Assam districts: **United Khasi-Jaintia Hills** and **Garo Hills** |
| Name | "Meghalaya" = *abode of clouds*, coined by geographer **Shiba Prasad (S.P.) Chatterjee** (compare Himalaya = abode of snow) |
| Capital | **Shillong** — "Scotland of the East" in British times |
| First Chief Minister | **Williamson A. Sangma** (2 Apr 1970 – 3 Mar 1978; CM of the autonomous state, then of the full state) |
| First Governor | **B.K. (Braj Kumar) Nehru** — also Governor of Assam; held Meghalaya 21 Jan 1972 – 18 Sep 1973 |
| High Court | **High Court of Meghalaya**, **23 March 2013** (NE Areas (Reorganisation) and Other Related Laws (Amendment) Act, 2012 — same law created the Manipur and Tripura HCs). Earlier: **Gauhati HC** |

> Do not memorise an ordinal such as "21st state" — sources number the NE states inconsistently.

### Legislature and representation

| Body | Numbers |
|---|---|
| Legislative Assembly | **60 seats, unicameral**; **55 reserved for ST**. 11th Assembly elected Feb 2023 — **NPP won 26** |
| Lok Sabha | **2** seats, both ST-reserved: **Shillong** and **Tura** |
| Rajya Sabha | **1** seat |

### Office holders (as of 27 Sep 2026)

| Post | Holder |
|---|---|
| Governor | **C.H. (Chandrashekhar H.) Vijayashankar** — sworn in 30 July 2024 |
| Chief Minister | **Conrad K. Sangma** (NPP) — second term (MDA-II) since March 2023 |
| Deputy CMs | **Prestone Tynsong** (Home-Police, PWD, District Council Affairs); **Sniawbhalang Dhar** (**Commerce & Industries**, Urban Affairs, Transport) — after the Sept 2025 reshuffle |
| Speaker | **Thomas A. Sangma** (NPP) — elected unopposed 9 Mar 2023 |
| Chief Justice, HC | **Justice Revati Mohite Dere** — sworn in 10 Jan 2026; second woman CJ of the court (predecessor Justice Soumen Sen moved to Kerala HC) |
| Lok Sabha MPs (2024) | **Shillong (ST): Dr Ricky Andrew J. Syngkon (VPP)**; **Tura (ST): Saleng A. Sangma (INC)** |
| Rajya Sabha MP | James P.K. Sangma (NPP), elected unopposed June 2026, succeeding Dr W.R. Kharlukhi |

### Sixth Schedule and the Autonomous District Councils (ADCs)

- Sixth Schedule basics (Arts 244(2) & 275(1), the four "AMTM" states, ADC powers, up to 30 members with not more than 4 nominated) — see *Indian Polity* module. Meghalaya has **3 of the 10 ADCs**:

| ADC | HQ | Formed | Seats |
|---|---|---|---|
| **KHADC** (Khasi Hills) | **Shillong** | **27 June 1952** — inaugurated by Assam Governor **Jairamdas Daulatram** as the *United Khasi-Jaintia Hills District Council*; renamed Khasi Hills DC in 1972–73 | **30** (29 elected + 1 nominated) |
| **JHADC** (Jaintia Hills) | **Jowai** | Jowai Autonomous District carved out **w.e.f. 1 Dec 1964**; first council session **8 Apr 1967**; renamed Jaintia Hills (notification 14 June 1973) | **30** (29 elected + 1 nominated) |
| **GHADC** (Garo Hills) | **Tura** | **1952** | **30** (29 elected + 1 nominated) |

> **Trap:** "All three ADCs were formed in 1952" is wrong — only KHADC and GHADC date from 1952; JHADC came from the 1964 split.

lessons.title: The 12 districts and their headquarters
lessons.body:
### The 12 districts (as of Sep 2026)

| # | District | Region | HQ | Created |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | East Khasi Hills | Khasi | **Shillong** | 1976 |
| 2 | West Khasi Hills | Khasi | **Nongstoin** | 1976 |
| 3 | East Garo Hills | Garo | **Williamnagar** | 1976 |
| 4 | West Garo Hills | Garo | **Tura** | 1976 |
| 5 | Ri-Bhoi | Khasi | **Nongpoh** | 1992 |
| 6 | South Garo Hills | Garo | **Baghmara** | 1992 |
| 7 | North Garo Hills | Garo | **Resubelpara** | 2012 (notified 26-07-2012) |
| 8 | East Jaintia Hills | Jaintia | **Khliehriat** | 2012 |
| 9 | West Jaintia Hills | Jaintia | **Jowai** | 2012 — the old Jaintia Hills district *renamed* |
| 10 | South West Khasi Hills | Khasi | **Mawkyrwat** | 2012 |
| 11 | South West Garo Hills | Garo | **Ampati** | 2012 |
| 12 | **Eastern West Khasi Hills** (newest) | Khasi | **Mairang** | **10 Nov 2021** — from the Mairang and Mawthadraishan C&RD blocks of West Khasi Hills |

- **By region:** Khasi Hills **5** (EKH, WKH, SWKH, EWKH, Ri-Bhoi) · Jaintia Hills **2** · Garo Hills **5**.
- **Most populous:** East Khasi Hills (8.26 lakh, Census 2011).
- No 13th district reported as of Sep 2026.

### Memory hooks for HQs

| Pair that gets swapped | Keep them apart |
|---|---|
| West Jaintia **Jowai** vs East Jaintia **Khliehriat** | Jowai is the old Jaintia HQ, so it stays with the "old" (renamed) district |
| West Khasi **Nongstoin** vs Eastern West Khasi **Mairang** | The 2021 child took the Mairang block — and its name |
| West Garo **Tura** vs East Garo **Williamnagar** | Tura = Garo Hills' big town (also GHADC HQ) |
| SW Garo **Ampati** vs SW Khasi **Mawkyrwat** | "**A**mpati — g**A**ro"; "**Maw**-" names cluster in the Khasi Hills (Mawsynram, Mawlynnong, Mawkyrwat) |
| North Garo **Resubelpara** vs South Garo **Baghmara** | Baghmara also has the Pitcher Plant Sanctuary and an LCS — both in the *south* |

> Creation waves: **1976** (4) → **1992** (Ri-Bhoi, South Garo) → **2012** (4 new + Jaintia renamed) → **2021** (Eastern West Khasi Hills).

lessons.title: Geography, rivers, caves & records
lessons.body:
### Basics

| Fact | Detail |
|---|---|
| Area | **22,429 km²** |
| Borders | **Assam** to the north and east; **Bangladesh** to the south and west |
| Plateau | **Meghalaya (Shillong) Plateau** — NE extension of the Peninsular plateau, separated from Chota Nagpur by the **Garo–Rajmahal (Malda) gap** |
| Hill regions (west → east) | **Garo – Khasi – Jaintia** |
| Highest peak | **Shillong Peak** (about 1,965 m — Meghalaya Tourism) |
| Highest in Garo Hills | **Nokrek Peak, 1,412 m** |
| Population 2011 | 29,66,889 · density 132/km² · **sex ratio 989** · literacy **74.43%** · **ST 86.15%** |
| Religion 2011 | Christian 74.59%, Hindu 11.52%, tribal religions 8.70%, Muslim 4.40% |

### Rivers

| River | Remember |
|---|---|
| **Simsang** (**Someshwari** in Bangladesh) | **Longest** river of Meghalaya; biggest in Garo Hills; rises in the Nokrek range, flows south |
| **Umngot** | Past **Dawki** (West Jaintia Hills); famed for crystal-clear water |
| **Umiam** | Dammed → **Umiam Lake (Barapani)**, 15 km N of Shillong. **Umiam Stage-I** (4×9 MW, 1965) = **first reservoir-based hydel project in NE India** |
| **Myntdu** | Past Jowai, through Leshka (hydel) into Bangladesh |
| **Kopili (Kupli)** | Part of the Jaintia Hills – Assam boundary |
| North-flowing (to Brahmaputra) | Khri, Umtrew, Umiam, Umkhen; Manda, Damring, **Jinjiram** (Garo) |
| South-flowing (to Bangladesh/Meghna) | Simsang, Bhogai, Kynshi, Umngot, Myntdu |

### Rainfall records (both places in East Khasi Hills)

| Record | Holder |
|---|---|
| Highest **average annual** rainfall (Guinness "wettest place") | **Mawsynram** — ~11,872 mm/yr (Guinness figure; IMD averages differ by period) |
| Most rain in a **calendar year** (Guinness) | **Mawsynram — 26,000 mm in 1985** |
| Most rain in **12 months** | **Sohra (Cherrapunji)**, Aug 1860 – Jul 1861 |
| Most rain in **one month** | **Sohra — 9,300 mm, July 1861** |

> Hook: **Mawsynram = the average champion; Sohra = the 1860–61 burst.**

### Caves and the Meghalayan Age

| Cave | Claim |
|---|---|
| **Krem Liat Prah** (East Jaintia Hills) | **Longest cave in India / South Asia**; big chamber "Aircraft Hangar" (length keeps growing as passages link — figures vary) |
| **Krem Puri** (Laitsohum, near Mawsynram) | **World's longest sandstone cave** — 24,583 m (2016 survey); mosasaur fossils; "fairy cave" |
| **Mawmluh Cave** (near Sohra) | Stalagmite defines the start of the **Meghalayan Age** — latest age of the **Holocene** (Greenlandian → Northgrippian → **Meghalayan**), began **4,200 years ago**, ratified **2018**. IUGS "First 100 Geological Heritage Sites" (Oct 2022) |
| Siju Cave | South Garo Hills |

### Living root bridges (Jingkieng Jri)
- Grown by Khasi and Jaintia communities from aerial roots of ***Ficus elastica*** (India rubber tree); 10–15 years to become usable; 70+ villages. Best known: **double-decker at Nongriat**.
- **UNESCO Tentative List 2022**; full nomination "Jingkieng Jri / Lyu Chrai Cultural Landscape" submitted **Jan 2026**; accepted as complete and due for decision at the **49th World Heritage Committee session in 2027** (as of Sep 2026).

### Protected areas

| Area | District | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **Balpakram NP** — "land of perpetual winds" | South Garo Hills | 220 km² |
| **Nokrek (Ridge) NP** | Garo Hills | 1986 |
| **Nokrek Biosphere Reserve** | Garo Hills | 820 km²; notified 1988; **UNESCO MAB 2009**; wild-citrus gene sanctuary; Hoolock gibbon |
| **Baghmara Pitcher Plant Sanctuary** | South Garo Hills | *Nepenthes khasiana* (endemic); 1984 |
| Siju WLS / Nongkhyllem WLS / Narpuh WLS | S. Garo / Ri-Bhoi / E. Jaintia | 1979 / 1981 / 2014 |

Totals: 2 NPs, 4 WLS, 1 BR ≈ 5.06% of the state.

### Superlatives and state symbols

| Item | Fact |
|---|---|
| **Nohkalikai Falls** (near Sohra) | **340 m** — India's **tallest plunge waterfall** |
| **Mawlynnong** (EKH) | "**Asia's cleanest village**" — *Discover India*, 2003 |
| **Kongthong** (EKH) | "**Whistling village**" (*Jingrwai Iawbei*); India's UNWTO Best Tourism Village entry 2021 |
| First **State Water Policy** in India | Meghalaya State Water Policy 2019 (Cabinet 12 July 2019) |
| State animal / bird / flower | **Clouded leopard** / **Hill myna** / **Lady's slipper orchid** |
| State tree / fish | Gamhar (*Gmelina arborea*) / chocolate mahseer |

lessons.title: People, matriliny & festivals
lessons.body:
### Communities

| Community | Language family | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **Khasi** | **Austroasiatic (Mon-Khmer)** | Largest group; 33.8% speakers (2011) |
| **Jaintia / Pnar** | Austroasiatic (Mon-Khmer) | Jaintia sub-group of the wider Khasi family; 10.7% |
| **Garo (A·chik)** | **Tibeto-Burman (Bodo-Garo)** | 31.6% |

Smaller groups: Hajong, Koch, Rabha, Biate, Boro, Rajbongshi, Karbi, Tiwa, Dimasa, Kuki, Nepali. Bengali speakers 6.4%.

### The matrilineal system

| | Khasi / Jaintia | Garo |
|---|---|---|
| Clan passes through | Mother — clan name **kur** | Mother — clan **ma·chong** |
| Heiress | **Youngest daughter, *Ka Khadduh*** — keeps the ancestral house and bulk of property, cares for parents | A daughter chosen by the parents (usually youngest) — **Nokna**; her husband = **Nokrom** |
| Husband | Usually moves into the wife's home | Nokrom lives in the Nokna's house |
| Sons | Do not inherit ancestral property | Do not inherit maternal property |

> **Matrilineal ≠ matriarchal.** Descent and inheritance run through the mother; political and clan authority traditionally lies with men (maternal uncles, the **Syiem**).

### Festivals and dances (months usually; exact dates follow lunar/clan calendars)

| Festival / dance | Community | Where | When | Remember |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Shad Suk Mynsiem** | **Khasi** | Shillong | **April** | "Dance of joyful hearts" — thanksgiving |
| **Ka Pomblang Nongkrem** (Shad Nongkrem) | **Khasi** (Hima Khyrim) | **Smit**, ~20 km from Shillong | **Oct–Nov**, ~5 days | Harvest thanksgiving of the Khyrim Syiemship |
| Shad Mastieh | Khasi | – | – | Warrior sword dance |
| **Behdienkhlam** | **Jaintia / Pnar** | **Jowai** | **July** | "Chasing away the demon of plague"; **Laho dance** performed |
| **Chad Sukra** | **Pnar** | Jaintia Hills | Spring (Apr–May), before sowing | No ploughing until it ends |
| **Wangala** — "**Hundred Drums**" | **Garo** | Garo Hills; 100 Drums gathering near **Tura** | **Oct–Nov** (post-harvest) | Thanksgiving to the sun god Saljong (commonly cited) |
| Rongchugala, Den Bilsia | Garo | Garo Hills | – | Agricultural festivals |

> **Not Meghalaya:** **Garia Puja** is a **Tripura** festival (April; Tripuri, Jamatia, Reang and other Kokborok-speaking tribes and the Halam; deity Baba Garia). It was a trap in the IPO 2022 paper — the "Gar-" sound pulls you towards Garo.

### Quick sort: which hill, which festival?
- **Khasi**: Shad Suk Mynsiem (Apr, Shillong), Nongkrem (Oct–Nov, Smit).
- **Jaintia/Pnar**: Behdienkhlam (Jul, Jowai), Chad Sukra (spring).
- **Garo**: Wangala (Oct–Nov, 100 drums).

lessons.title: History & freedom fighters
lessons.body:
### Resistance heroes — the martyrs' column in Shillong honours all three

| Hero | Community | Key facts | Remembered on |
|---|---|---|---|
| **U Tirot Sing** | Khasi — **Syiem of Nongkhlaw** | Led the **Anglo-Khasi War (1829–1833)**, sparked in April 1829 by the British **Guwahati–Sylhet road** through Nongkhlaw. Captured 1833; **died in Dhaka jail, 17 July 1835**. Statue unveiled in Dhaka in 2024 | **17 July** — U Tirot Sing Day (state holiday) |
| **U Kiang Nangbah** | Jaintia (Pnar) | Led the **Jaintia rebellion (1860–62)**; **hanged publicly at Iawmusiang, Jowai, 30 Dec 1862** | **30 December** |
| **Pa Togan Nengminza Sangma** | Garo | Night attack on a British camp during the Garo resistance; **killed 12 Dec 1872** | **12 December** — Pa Togan Day |

> Hook: **K → J → G = 35 → 62 → 72.** Khasi hero died 1835, Jaintia hero 1862, Garo hero 1872 — each date is roughly a generation after the last.

### Timeline to statehood

| Year | Event |
|---|---|
| 1829–33 | Anglo-Khasi War (U Tirot Sing) |
| 1860–62 | Jaintia rebellion (U Kiang Nangbah) |
| 1872 | Pa Togan Sangma killed resisting the British in the Garo Hills |
| British era | Shillong called "Scotland of the East" |
| 27 June 1952 | United Khasi-Jaintia Hills District Council inaugurated (Sixth Schedule) |
| 1 Dec 1964 | Jowai Autonomous District carved out (later JHADC) |
| 1969 | 22nd Amendment — Art. 244A; Assam Reorganisation (Meghalaya) Act |
| 2 Apr 1970 | Autonomous State within Assam; CM Williamson A. Sangma |
| 21 Jan 1972 | Full state (with Manipur, Tripura) — Meghalaya Day |
| 7 Nov 1972 | North Eastern Council (NEC Act, 1971) comes into being, HQ **Shillong** |
| 23 Mar 2013 | Own High Court |

lessons.title: Economy, minerals & GI tags
lessons.body:
### Minerals

| Mineral | Facts |
|---|---|
| **Coal** | Mainly **Jaintia Hills** (East Jaintia Hills), also Khasi & Garo Hills. **576.48 MT** resources (GSI inventory, 1 Apr 2021). Traditionally **rat-hole mining** |
| Coal ban timeline | **NGT ban: 17 Apr 2014** → Dec 2018 Ksan (East Jaintia Hills) mine flooding → **July 2019 Supreme Court** allows mining by scientific methods with approved plans → **scientific mining starts after permissions in Jan 2025**. Illegal mining still reported |
| **Limestone** | Very large, high-grade reserves in the **southern Khasi-Jaintia belt** (Lumshnong, Sohra/Mawmluh) — basis of the **cement** industry |
| **Uranium** | **Domiasiat / Kylleng-Pyndengsohiong-Mawthabah (KPM)**, **West Khasi Hills** — UCIL's sandstone-type deposit, described as India's largest near-surface sandstone-type uranium deposit |
| Others | **Sillimanite (Sonapahar, West Khasi Hills)**, kaolin/china clay, granite, quartz, glass sand |

### Agriculture and horticulture
- Mostly agrarian; **jhum (shifting cultivation)** still practised, especially in Garo Hills.
- Crops: rice, maize, potato, ginger, **turmeric**, pineapple, **Khasi mandarin**, banana, black pepper, areca nut, strawberry.
- **Lakadong turmeric** (**West Jaintia Hills**): curcumin **6.5–7.5%** vs 2–3% in common varieties. **Mission Lakadong (2018–2023)** — target 50,000 MT/yr. **Mission Golden Spice** (MDoNER + State, launched **21 Jul 2026**): ₹175.45 cr, five-year (2025–2030) Lakadong value-chain project.

### GI tags of Meghalaya

| GI product | Type | Year |
|---|---|---|
| **Khasi Mandarin** | Agricultural | 2014–15 |
| **Memong Narang** (wild orange, Garo Hills) | Agricultural | 2015–16 |
| **Lakadong Turmeric** | Agricultural | **2024** |
| **Garo Dakmanda** (women's wrap-around; registered as *Meghalaya Garo Textile*) | Handicraft/textile | **2024** |
| **Larnai (Lyrnai) Pottery** (black pottery, Jaintia Hills; registered as *Meghalaya Lyrnai Pottery*) | Handicraft | **2024** |
| **Garo Chubitchi** (rice brew; registered as *Meghalaya Chubitchi*) | Manufactured | **2024** |
| **Meghalaya Ryndia** (**Eri silk** textile) | Handloom | **2 Apr 2025** |

- ~32 more products have applications pending (as of May 2026): Sohra honey, Meghalaya pineapple, black pepper, Tungrymbai, Garo sticky rice.
- **Umden-Diwon** (Ri-Bhoi) — Meghalaya's **first Eri Silk Village**, 12 Feb 2021.

> Hook for the 2024 batch: **"LLDC"** — **L**akadong, **L**arnai, **D**akmanda, **C**hubitchi.

### Economic target
- **Mission 10**: a **USD 10 billion economy by 2028** (baseline GSDP 2022-23 ₹42,697 cr; 2024-25 projected ₹52,973 cr).

lessons.title: Current Meghalaya affairs 2025–26 (as of Sep 2026)
lessons.body:
All items **as of 27 Sep 2026**.

### Governance and law

| Date | Development |
|---|---|
| **16 / 27 Apr 2026** | Cabinet approval, then Governor's **Meghalaya Official Languages Ordinance, 2026** (Art. **213(1)**): **English, Khasi and Garo** all official languages (from a notified date); **Meghalaya State Language Act, 2005** (Khasi/Garo only *associate* official) repealed |
| **13 / 28 Aug 2026** | Cabinet approved, then the Assembly **passed**, the **Meghalaya Official Languages Bill, 2026**, replacing the Ordinance |
| July 2018 (background) | Assembly resolution seeking **8th Schedule** status for Khasi and Garo — not yet included |
| **10 Jan 2026** | **Justice Revati Mohite Dere** sworn in as Chief Justice — second woman CJ of the Meghalaya HC |
| June 2026 | Rajya Sabha: James P.K. Sangma (NPP) elected unopposed |
| Sept 2025 | Cabinet reshuffle — Deputy CM **Sniawbhalang Dhar** holds **Commerce & Industries** |
| **13 Aug 2026** | Cabinet: new **MCS Paper VI on Meghalaya** (history, culture, traditional systems, society, economy); Bill to amend the **Meghalaya GST Act, 2017** (passed by the Assembly 28 Aug 2026) |

### Environment, mining and resources

| Date | Development |
|---|---|
| **26 Aug 2026** | Assembly **unanimously (all 60 MLAs)** passed CM Conrad Sangma's resolution asking the Centre, DAE and UCIL **not to allow uranium exploration/mining** — specifically opposing the **KPM** project |
| Jan 2025 | **Scientific coal mining** begins after permissions (NGT ban since 2014) |
| Mar 2025 | **IQAir World Air Quality Report 2024**: **Byrnihat** (Ri-Bhoi, Assam–Meghalaya border industrial town) = **world's most polluted metropolitan area**, PM2.5 **128.2 µg/m³**; the state disputed it and shut six ferro-alloy units |
| 24 Mar 2026 | **IQAir report for 2025**: **Loni** (Ghaziabad, UP) = world's most polluted city (PM2.5 112.5 µg/m³); Byrnihat still among the world's 10 most polluted |
| Monsoon 2025 | Sohra ~50% below normal; Surlabbi (Karnataka) topped Jun–Jul 2025 totals — a seasonal anomaly, not a change in the records |

### Culture, sport and economy

| Date | Development |
|---|---|
| Jan 2026 | India submitted the **living root bridges** nomination ("Jingkieng Jri / Lyu Chrai Cultural Landscape") to UNESCO; decision due at the 49th World Heritage Committee session, **2027** |
| **2 Apr 2025** | **Meghalaya Ryndia** (Eri silk) gets GI tag |
| **21 Jul 2026** | **Mission Golden Spice** launched by MDoNER and the State — ₹175.45 cr, 2025–2030, for the GI-tagged **Lakadong turmeric** value chain |
| 2027 | Meghalaya to host the **39th National Games** (Feb–Mar 2027 window per the IOA; host-state agreement signed 30 May 2026) — first time; venues **Shillong** (JN Stadium), **Tura** (P.A. Sangma Stadium), **Jowai** |
| **23 Sep 2026** | CM inaugurated **Shillong Technology Park Phase-II** at New Shillong Township, Umsawli (₹121 cr) |

### Inter-state boundary
- **29 Mar 2022**: Assam–Meghalaya MoU in New Delhi (in Amit Shah's presence) settled **6 of the 12 "areas of difference"** — Tarabari, Gizang, Hahim, Boklapara, Khanapara-Pilangkata, Ratacherra — about **70%** of the border.
- **Pending six** (second-phase talks unresolved as of Sep 2026): Langpih, Borduar, Nongwah-Mawtamur, Desh Doomreah, Block I & II, Psiar-Khanduli.

examples.q: How to crack a district-HQ question — e.g. 'Khliehriat is the headquarters of: (a) West Jaintia Hills (b) East Jaintia Hills (c) Ri-Bhoi (d) South West Khasi Hills'
examples.solution:
Step 1: Place the name in its hill region. 'Khlieh-' is a Jaintia name; Ri-Bhoi (Nongpoh) and SW Khasi (Mawkyrwat) drop out.
Step 2: Jaintia Hills has only two districts. Jowai was the old Jaintia HQ, and the old district was renamed West Jaintia Hills in 2012 — so Jowai stays with the West.
Step 3: The new 2012 district, East Jaintia Hills, got Khliehriat.
Answer: (b) East Jaintia Hills
examples.shortcut: For every 'split' district the parent keeps the old town (Jowai, Nongstoin, Tura) and the child gets the new one (Khliehriat, Mairang, Ampati/Resubelpara).

examples.q: How to crack festival ↔ community questions — e.g. 'Behdienkhlam is celebrated by the: (a) Garos (b) Pnars (c) Khasis of Smit (d) Tripuris'
examples.solution:
Step 1: Recall the anchor town. Behdienkhlam = Jowai, July.
Step 2: Jowai is the Jaintia (Pnar) heartland, not Khasi (Shillong/Smit) or Garo (Tura).
Step 3: Tripuris are a Tripura community (Garia Puja) — a distractor.
Answer: (b) Pnars
examples.shortcut: Tie each festival to one town: Shad Suk Mynsiem → Shillong, Nongkrem → Smit, Behdienkhlam → Jowai, Wangala → Tura. Town → hill region → community.

examples.q: How to crack rainfall-record questions — 'Which place holds the record for the highest rainfall in a single calendar month? (a) Mawsynram (b) Sohra (c) Agumbe (d) Pasighat'
examples.solution:
Step 1: Separate the two record types. Mawsynram owns the AVERAGE annual record (Guinness) and the 1985 calendar-year record.
Step 2: Sohra owns the historical burst records of 1860–61: 12 months (Aug 1860 – Jul 1861) and one month (9,300 mm in July 1861).
Step 3: 'Single month' is a burst record → Sohra.
Answer: (b) Sohra (Cherrapunji)

examples.q: How to crack a Sixth Schedule / ADC question — 'Which statement is correct? (a) All three ADCs of Meghalaya were set up in 1952 (b) JHADC has its HQ at Jowai (c) The Sixth Schedule applies to Manipur (d) ADCs work under the Fifth Schedule'
examples.solution:
Step 1: Sixth Schedule states = Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram (AMTM). Manipur is not one → (c) wrong; (d) wrong schedule.
Step 2: KHADC and GHADC date from 1952, but the Jowai Autonomous District was carved out only w.e.f. 1 Dec 1964 → (a) wrong.
Step 3: JHADC HQ is Jowai.
Answer: (b)
examples.shortcut: Sixth = AMTM; the three ADCs sit in the three regional towns: Shillong, Jowai, Tura.

examples.q: How to crack GI-tag questions — 'Which of these Meghalaya products did NOT receive a GI tag in 2024? (a) Lakadong turmeric (b) Larnai pottery (c) Khasi mandarin (d) Garo Dakmanda'
examples.solution:
Step 1: Recall the 2024 batch with the hook LLDC: Lakadong, Larnai, Dakmanda, Chubitchi.
Step 2: Khasi mandarin is the oldest Meghalaya GI (2014–15), with Memong Narang (2015–16).
Step 3: Ryndia (Eri silk) came later, on 2 Apr 2025.
Answer: (c) Khasi mandarin
examples.shortcut: Oranges are old (2014–16), LLDC is 2024, Ryndia is 2025.

traps: Festival ↔ community swaps: Behdienkhlam (Jowai, July) and Chad Sukra are Jaintia/Pnar — not Garo; Wangala (100 drums, Oct–Nov) is Garo — not Khasi; Shad Suk Mynsiem (April) and Nongkrem (Smit) are Khasi. Garia Puja is Tripura, not Garo — the IPO 2022 paper used exactly this sound-alike.

District HQ swaps: West Jaintia = Jowai but East Jaintia = Khliehriat; West Khasi = Nongstoin but Eastern West Khasi (2021) = Mairang; West Garo = Tura but East Garo = Williamnagar; South West Garo = Ampati but South West Khasi = Mawkyrwat; North Garo = Resubelpara, South Garo = Baghmara. The parent district keeps the old town.

Mawsynram vs Sohra: Mawsynram has the highest AVERAGE annual rainfall (Guinness) and the 1985 calendar-year record; Sohra holds the 12-month (1860–61) and single-month (July 1861) records. A dry 2025 monsoon at Sohra did not change any record.

Two dates for statehood: 2 April 1970 = autonomous state within Assam (22nd Amendment, Art. 244A); 21 January 1972 = full state (NE Areas Reorganisation Act 1971) — Meghalaya Day, shared with Manipur and Tripura. Do not pick 26 January or 1969 (the Amendment year).

Inheritance words: Ka Khadduh = Khasi youngest-daughter heiress; Nokna = Garo heiress and Nokrom = her husband; Syiem = Khasi chief (male). Matrilineal ≠ matriarchal — authority stays largely with men. Also: Krem Liat Prah = longest cave in South Asia, Krem Puri = longest SANDSTONE cave in the world, Mawmluh = Meghalayan Age stalagmite — three different caves.

practice.q: Meghalaya attained full statehood on
practice.explanation:
The North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971 made Meghalaya a full state on 21 Jan 1972 (Meghalaya Day, shared with Manipur and Tripura). 2 Apr 1970 was the autonomous-state date.
Hook: '69 → 70 → 72' — Amendment, autonomy, statehood.

practice.q: Which constitutional amendment inserted Article 244A, enabling the creation of an autonomous State (Meghalaya) within Assam?
practice.explanation:
The 22nd Amendment Act, 1969 added Art. 244A; the Assam Reorganisation (Meghalaya) Act, 1969 followed, and the autonomous state began on 2 Apr 1970.
Hook: 22nd → 244A — 'twenty-two, two-forty-four-A'.

practice.q: The name 'Meghalaya' (abode of clouds) was coined by
practice.explanation:
Geographer Shiba Prasad (S.P.) Chatterjee coined the name. B.K. Nehru was the first Governor; Williamson A. Sangma the first CM.
Hook: Himalaya = abode of snow, Meghalaya = abode of clouds — a geographer's word-play.

practice.q: Who was the first Chief Minister of Meghalaya?
practice.explanation:
Williamson A. Sangma was CM from 2 Apr 1970 (autonomous state) to 3 Mar 1978. Conrad K. Sangma is the current CM (as of Sep 2026).
Hook: one CM bridged both stages — autonomous state (1970) and full state (1972).

practice.q: How many districts does Meghalaya have (as of 2026)?
practice.explanation:
12 districts; the newest, Eastern West Khasi Hills (HQ Mairang), was created on 10 Nov 2021. Region split: Khasi 5, Jaintia 2, Garo 5.
Hook: 5 + 2 + 5 = 12.
practice.note: As of Sep 2026; changes if a new district is created.

practice.q: The headquarters of Eastern West Khasi Hills district is
practice.explanation:
Mairang. The district was carved from West Khasi Hills (HQ Nongstoin) on 10 Nov 2021 out of the Mairang and Mawthadraishan blocks.
Hook: the child took the Mairang block — and made it its HQ.

practice.q: Khliehriat is the headquarters of which district?
practice.explanation:
East Jaintia Hills (created 2012). West Jaintia Hills — the renamed old Jaintia Hills district — kept Jowai.
Hook: the parent keeps the old town (Jowai); the new district gets the new HQ (Khliehriat).

practice.q: The highest peak of Meghalaya is
practice.explanation:
Shillong Peak (about 1,965 m per Meghalaya Tourism). Nokrek (1,412 m) is the highest in the Garo Hills.
Hook: the capital sits under the state's highest point.

practice.q: Which is the longest river of Meghalaya, known as the Someshwari in Bangladesh?
practice.explanation:
The Simsang rises in the Nokrek range (Garo Hills) and flows south into Bangladesh as the Someshwari.
Hook: 'Simsang = Someshwari' — both start with S.

practice.q: The crystal-clear Umngot river flows past which border town?
practice.explanation:
Dawki (West Jaintia Hills), also the site of the Dawki–Tamabil land port/ICP. Dalu, Baghmara and Borsora are other Land Customs Stations.
Hook: Umngot + Dawki = clear water and the land port — Jaintia Hills' window to Bangladesh.

practice.q: Guinness World Records lists which place as receiving the highest average annual rainfall?
practice.explanation:
Mawsynram (~11,872 mm/yr, Guinness figure). Sohra holds the one-month (July 1861) and 12-month (1860–61) records.
Hook: 'Average → Mawsynram; 1861 → Sohra'.

practice.q: The youngest geological age of the Holocene, ratified in 2018, is named after Meghalaya because its reference stalagmite came from
practice.explanation:
A Mawmluh Cave stalagmite (near Sohra) marks the start of the Meghalayan Age, 4,200 years ago (after the Greenlandian and Northgrippian).
Hook: 'Mawmluh marks the Meghalayan' — M-M.

practice.q: Krem Puri in Meghalaya is famous as the world's longest cave made of
practice.explanation:
Krem Puri (Laitsohum, near Mawsynram) is the world's longest sandstone cave, 24,583 m (2016 survey); mosasaur fossils were found in it.
Hook: 'Puri = pure sand'.

practice.q: Which is the longest known cave in India / South Asia?
practice.explanation:
Krem Liat Prah in East Jaintia Hills; its huge chamber is nicknamed the 'Aircraft Hangar'. Its surveyed length keeps growing as passages are linked.
Hook: Liat Prah = longest; Puri = sandstone; Mawmluh = Meghalayan Age.

practice.q: The living root bridges of Meghalaya (Jingkieng Jri) are grown from the roots of
practice.explanation:
Ficus elastica (India rubber tree). The bridges have been on UNESCO's Tentative List since 2022; India submitted the full nomination in Jan 2026; UNESCO is due to decide in 2027 (as of Sep 2026).
Hook: 'elastic roots stretch across streams'.

practice.q: India's first state to adopt its own State Water Policy was
practice.explanation:
Meghalaya State Water Policy, 2019 (Cabinet approval 12 July 2019).
Hook: the wettest state wrote the first water policy.

practice.q: Nokrek Biosphere Reserve was included in UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves in
practice.explanation:
UNESCO MAB, 2009 (it was notified as a biosphere reserve in 1988). Known for a wild-citrus gene sanctuary and Hoolock gibbons.
Hook: 'Nokrek — nine (2009)'.

practice.q: The state animal of Meghalaya is the
practice.explanation:
Clouded leopard; state bird hill myna; state flower lady's slipper orchid.
Hook: the abode of clouds has a clouded leopard.

practice.q: Among the Khasis, the youngest daughter who inherits the ancestral property is called
practice.explanation:
Ka Khadduh. Among the Garos the heiress is the Nokna and her husband the Nokrom; a Syiem is a (male) Khasi chief.
Hook: 'Khadduh — Khasi'; 'Nok- — Garo'.

practice.q: Wangala, the 'Festival of Hundred Drums', is celebrated by the
practice.explanation:
Wangala is the Garo post-harvest thanksgiving (Oct–Nov); the '100 Drums' gathering is held near Tura.
Hook: 'Wangala — the Garo drum-gala'.

practice.q: Behdienkhlam, celebrated at Jowai in July, is a festival of the
practice.explanation:
A Jaintia/Pnar festival to 'chase away the demon of plague'; the Laho dance is performed at it.
Hook: Jowai → Jaintia → Behdienkhlam (July).

practice.q: The Nongkrem dance festival (Ka Pomblang Nongkrem) of the Khasis is held at
practice.explanation:
Smit, seat of Hima Khyrim, about 20 km from Shillong, usually in Oct–Nov (about 5 days).
Hook: 'Nongkrem at Smit — Khyrim's harvest hit'.

practice.q: Shad Suk Mynsiem, the 'Dance of the Peaceful Hearts' held in Shillong in spring, is a traditional dance of the
practice.explanation:
Shad Suk Mynsiem is a Khasi thanksgiving dance, held in Shillong in April (Meghalaya Tourism). Wangala is Garo; Behdienkhlam is Jaintia/Pnar.
Hook: 'Suk = peace; Shillong = Khasi'.

practice.q: U Tirot Sing, who led the Anglo-Khasi War (1829–33), was the Syiem of
practice.explanation:
Syiem of Nongkhlaw; the war began over the British Guwahati–Sylhet road through Nongkhlaw. He died in Dhaka jail on 17 July 1835 (U Tirot Sing Day).
Hook: 'Tirot of Nongkhlaw — the road through his land started the war'.

practice.q: U Kiang Nangbah was publicly hanged by the British at Iawmusiang, Jowai, on
practice.explanation:
30 Dec 1862, after the Jaintia uprising of 1860–62. 17 July 1835 = Tirot Sing's death; 12 Dec 1872 = Pa Togan's death.
Hook: K → J → G = 35 → 62 → 72.

practice.q: Pa Togan Nengminza Sangma, the Garo freedom fighter, was killed fighting the British on
practice.explanation:
12 Dec 1872, observed as Pa Togan Day.
Hook: K → J → G = 35 → 62 → 72 — the Garo hero is last.

practice.q: The Autonomous District Councils of Meghalaya function under which Schedule of the Constitution?
practice.explanation:
The Sixth Schedule (Art. 244(2), 275(1)) — KHADC (Shillong), JHADC (Jowai), GHADC (Tura). It covers Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
Hook: Sixth = 'AMTM'.

practice.q: How many seats does the Meghalaya Legislative Assembly have, and how many of them are reserved for STs?
practice.explanation:
60 seats, 55 ST-reserved (unicameral). The state has 2 Lok Sabha seats (Shillong, Tura — both ST) and 1 Rajya Sabha seat.
Hook: 60 − 5 = 55.

practice.q: The High Court of Meghalaya was established on
practice.explanation:
23 Mar 2013, under the North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) and Other Related Laws (Amendment) Act, 2012; until then Meghalaya came under the Gauhati High Court.
Hook: statehood '72, own High Court '13 — 41 years later.

practice.q: Under the Meghalaya Official Languages Ordinance, 2026, the official languages of the State are
practice.explanation:
Promulgated 27 Apr 2026 under Art. 213(1); it repealed the Meghalaya State Language Act, 2005, under which Khasi and Garo were only associate official languages (source: newsonair.gov.in, Apr 2026).
Hook: 'Associate → full' — English keeps its place, Khasi and Garo join it.
practice.note: The Meghalaya Official Languages Bill, 2026, replacing the Ordinance, was passed by the Assembly on 28 Aug 2026 (as of Sep 2026).

practice.q: Lakadong turmeric, which received a GI tag in 2024, comes from which district of Meghalaya?
practice.explanation:
West Jaintia Hills; its curcumin content is about 6.5–7.5% against 2–3% in common varieties. Mission Lakadong ran 2018–2023.
Hook: 'LLDC' = the 2024 GI batch — Lakadong, Larnai, Dakmanda, Chubitchi.

practice.q: 'Ryndia', which received a GI tag in 2025, is a Meghalaya textile made from
practice.explanation:
Eri silk ('Meghalaya Ryndia', GI tag announced 2 Apr 2025). Umden-Diwon (Ri-Bhoi) is the state's first Eri Silk Village (2021).
Hook: 'Ryndia = Eri-ndia'.

practice.q: The Kylleng-Pyndengsohiong-Mawthabah (KPM) project in West Khasi Hills relates to mining of
practice.explanation:
A UCIL uranium project in the Domiasiat area. On 26 Aug 2026 the Assembly unanimously resolved against uranium exploration and mining (Shillong Times, 27 Aug 2026).
Hook: 'Domiasiat — the atom's seat'.

practice.q: The National Green Tribunal banned rat-hole coal mining in Meghalaya in
practice.explanation:
17 Apr 2014. The Ksan mine flooding was in Dec 2018; the Supreme Court allowed scientific mining in July 2019; scientific mining began after permissions in Jan 2025.
Hook: 2014 ban → 2019 SC → 2025 restart.

practice.q: Which Meghalaya village was called 'Asia's cleanest village' by Discover India magazine in 2003?
practice.explanation:
Mawlynnong (East Khasi Hills). Kongthong is the 'whistling village'; Nongriat has the double-decker root bridge.
Hook: Mawlynnong = clean (2003); Kongthong = whistle; Nongriat = double-decker bridge.

practice.q: Meghalaya will host which edition of the National Games in 2027?
practice.explanation:
The 39th National Games (Feb–Mar 2027 per the IOA) — the state's first time as host; venues Shillong, Tura and Jowai (olympics.com, IOA).
Hook: 3 venues, 39th Games.

practice.q: Who is the Governor of Meghalaya (as of September 2026)?
practice.explanation:
C.H. (Chandrashekhar H.) Vijayashankar, sworn in 30 July 2024 (Highland Post, Jul 2024). B.K. Nehru was the first Governor; Thomas A. Sangma is Speaker; Prestone Tynsong is a Deputy CM.
Hook: first Governor B.K. Nehru (1972) vs current Governor Vijayashankar (2024) — don't mix the two ends of the list.

practice.q: Byrnihat, named the world's most polluted metropolitan area in IQAir's World Air Quality Report 2024, lies in which district of Meghalaya?
practice.explanation:
Ri-Bhoi, on the Assam–Meghalaya border; annual PM2.5 was 128.2 µg/m³ (IQAir report released Mar 2025). The state disputed the finding and shut six ferro-alloy units.
Hook: 'Byrnihat — burning at the border (Ri-Bhoi)'.
practice.note: The title is for 2024 data. In IQAir's report for 2025 (24 Mar 2026), Loni (Ghaziabad, UP) was the most polluted city; Byrnihat stayed in the world's top 10 (as of Sep 2026).

practice.q: The Assam–Meghalaya boundary MoU signed on 29 March 2022 settled how many of the 12 'areas of difference'?
practice.explanation:
6 of 12 (Tarabari, Gizang, Hahim, Boklapara, Khanapara-Pilangkata, Ratacherra) — about 70% of the border. Six remain (as of Sep 2026), including Langpih and Block I & II (PIB, Mar 2022).
Hook: 'half settled' — 6 of 12.

practice.q: Which Autonomous District Council of Meghalaya was NOT set up in 1952?
options: All three were set up in 1952
practice.explanation:
JHADC: the Jowai Autonomous District was carved out of the United Khasi-Jaintia Hills district w.e.f. 1 Dec 1964, and its council first sat on 8 Apr 1967. KHADC (27 June 1952) and GHADC (1952) are the originals.
Hook: 'Jaintia came later' — J after K and G.
